engine.description: Engine of the global operations (aggregate, sort). auto: pandas, except beyond HYDRA_LARGE_VOLUME_ROWS estimated rows (2,000,000): the large-volume engine (pyarrow + DuckDB, extra hydra-etl[duckdb]). The HYDRA_ENGINE variable takes precedence.

steps.description: Ordered list of steps, each one an object with ONE key only: the name of the operation.

aggregate.title: AggregateOp

clean.description: Cleans text columns: spaces (trim + repeated spaces) and case.
clean.title: CleanOp

join.description:
Join with a reference source (a second flow).

YAML parameters:
    join:
      right:                    # the reference source, declared like a source
        type: mysql
        connection: {...}
        extract: {table: departments}
      key: email                # common key (a string or a list of strings)
      how: left                 # inner | left | right | outer | cross

how: cross: cartesian product (every row x every right row), no key;
max_rows guard (default 10,000,000 rows produced).

max_rows.description: how: cross only. Maximum rows produced (default 10,000,000).
max_rows.title: Max Rows

join.title: JoinOp

merge.description: SQL Server style merge (upsert of the target from the source, on a key).
merge.title: MergeOp

script.description:
Custom Python transformation (like an SSIS Script Component).

The user declares a contract (input columns -> output columns) and gives a
Python snippet, run in a restricted environment.

YAML parameters:
    script:
      inputs: [price, quantity]      # columns read (contract)
      outputs:                       # columns produced (+ type)
        total: float
        label: str
      mode: vectorized               # vectorized | row
      code: |
        total = price * quantity
        label = "big" if total.iloc[0] > 100 else "small"

Modes:
- vectorized: each input column is a pandas.Series;
              the code must assign every output column (Series or scalar).
- row:        the code runs row by row (like SSIS ProcessInputRow);
              each input column is a scalar.

Allowed output types: int, float, str, bool, date, datetime, any.
script.title: ScriptOp

text_to_rows.description:
One row per value of a text column ("a;b;c" -> 3 rows, other columns copied).
A null value, or one with no non-empty part, keeps one row with a null value.

    text_to_rows:
      column: tags          # column to split (required)
      sep: ";"              # separator (default ","), plain text
      regex: false          # true: sep is a regular expression
      trim: true            # strip spaces around each value
      keep_empty: false     # empty values are dropped
      index_column: tag_pos # optional: position 1, 2, 3...
text_to_rows.title: TextToRowsOp

union.description: Union / Union All: stacks a second source (same columns).
union.title: UnionOp

WindowColumn.description: A column added by window: its function and options.

col.description: Column read by the function (not for row_number, rank, dense_rank).
col.title: Col

default.description: lag / lead: value when the offset leaves the partition (default null).
default.title: Default

offset.description: lag / lead: rows to look back or ahead (default 1).
offset.title: Offset

WindowColumn.title: WindowColumn

WindowOrderItem.description: Item of window.order_by written as {col, desc}.
WindowOrderItem.title: WindowOrderItem

window.description:
Window functions: adds columns and keeps every row, in its input order.
Rank (row_number, rank, dense_rank), offset (lag, lead), running (cumsum,
cumcount, cummin, cummax) and whole-partition (sum, mean, min, max, count,
first, last) functions. Rank, offset and running functions need order_by.
Full rules: internal/engines/window.py.

columns.description: Mapping of output_column: {func, col, offset, default}.
columns.title: Columns

order_by.description: Order inside each partition: names or {col, desc}; nulls last, ties in input order.
order_by.title: Order By

partition_by.description: Columns splitting the rows into independent partitions (whole table without it).
partition_by.title: Partition By

window.title: WindowOp

transformations.description: Nested form, equivalent to 'steps' at the root.
